idiom_name: new Writable({ highWaterMark }) with typed chunk and 'drain' handling
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds no runtime behaviour here, so the realization is Node's contract with types attached: the Writable's highWaterMark is the buffer bound, write() returns a boolean that is false once the bound is reached, and the 'drain' event (or writableNeedDrain) is the resume signal, all of it described in @types/node. The types earn their keep when the policy is named in the domain - a FullPolicy union or an explicit result type makes 'the item was refused' something callers must handle rather than an ignored boolean. Where Node streams are unavailable (browsers, workers, edge runtimes) or the queue holds values rather than bytes, the same contract is written by hand as a small generic queue.
pitfalls: The typed boolean is easy to discard: `void out.write(x)` type-checks and deletes the bound, so lint or wrap the write in a helper that handles false.

highWaterMark is a threshold rather than a limit, and its unit depends on mode (bytes, objects, UTF-16 units) - an untyped {"highWaterMark": "64kb"} from config silently disables or inflates the bound.
Calling write() after end() (or from several async callers without awaiting) produces ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END or interleaved chunks; the bound does not protect ordering.

variants.name: Generic BoundedQueue<T> with a FullPolicy union
variants.implementation_notes: Where the platform's stream types are absent or the buffer holds values rather than bytes, the pattern is a small generic class: a fixed-length array or ring with push/pop, a FullPolicy union selected in the constructor, and a discriminated result from tryPush so the compiler forces the caller to deal with a refusal. This is the runtime-agnostic realization (browsers, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, test doubles), and it is also the point where a typed language pays off: 'evicted' is data, not a side effect, so a drop-oldest policy can hand the lost item back for logging or compensation. Prefer the platform primitives when they exist; hand-roll when the policy, the accounting or the runtime requires it.
variants.idiom_name: class BoundedQueue<T> with a discriminated result from tryPush
pitfalls: Types are erased: a policy string coming from configuration or an any-cast is not validated at runtime, so the constructor must reject unknown policy values.
A single-threaded runtime has no data races but does have await interleaving: checking length and pushing in different ticks still admits too many items - keep both in one synchronous block.
Generics give no thread or process safety: a queue shared across workers requires structured cloning or a message channel, not a shared instance.
